items.title: Hegseth Touts Americas Counter Cartel Coalition During Panama Visit

items.content_text: Following the recent second meeting of the Angola–United States Joint Defense Cooperation Committee, the parties intend to pursue a closer security relationship and meet again in 2028.

items.title: Joint Base Andrews to gain HH-60W, 5th Helicopter Squadron to support contingency response operations
items.content_text: The Department of the Air Force has selected Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, as the preferred location to replace the existing 26 UH-1N “Huey” helicopters with 26 HH-60W helicopters. Andrews will stand up the 5th Helicopter Squadron, the first unit on base to receive the HH-60W.

items.title: CMSAF announces EPME Modernization, additional enlisted force initiatives at AFSA Summit
items.content_text: During his keynote address at AFSA Summit 26, Chief Master Sergeant of the Air Force David R. Wolfe unveiled a sweeping overhaul of enlisted professional development, alongside key updates to promotion processes and spouse employment support.

items.title: ManTech Marks 70 Years of Creating Innovative Military Solutions
items.content_text: The War Department marked the 70th anniversary of its Manufacturing Technology enterprise, which solves challenges beyond industry partners' investment capacity and risk tolerance, by showcasing the program's innovative technologies during events at the Pentagon.

items.content_text: The DAF has streamlined its COVID-19 reinstatement process by establishing parallel processing for medical screening and military record correction board actions alongside deploying dedicated reinstatement case managers.

items.title: FBI Operation Steadfast Promise Targets Violent Crime in Indian Country
items.content_text: As part of Operation Steadfast Promise, a sustained commitment to address violent crime and improve public safety in Indian country, the FBI has concentrated efforts to combat criminal gangs and criminal enterprises that have exploited Tribal lands and communities.

items.title: U.S., Moroccan Forces Leverage Africa's Multidomain Experimentation Center
items.content_text: U.S. service members partnered with Morocco's royal armed forces to enable the first-ever live-fire demonstration leveraging the Africa Multidomain Training and Experimentation Center, supporting a U.S. defense industry partner in testing long-range precision-strike capabilities as part of the Army's Test Range Expansion Initiative.

items.title: Hegseth Renames Joint Base Charleston to Honor Late Sen. Lindsey Graham
items.content_text: Joint Base Charleston, S.C., became Joint Base Lindsey Graham during a ceremony to rename the installation after the late senator, Air Force veteran and South Carolina native son.

items.title: USS Thomas Hudner Returns to Naval Station Mayport From Deployment
items.content_text: The guided-missile destroyer USS Thomas Hudner returned to Naval Station Mayport, Fla., concluding an almost nine-month deployment across multiple geographic theaters, including the U.S. 4th, 5th and 6th Fleet areas of operations.

items.title: Medal of Honor Monday: Army Sgt. William Shemin
items.content_text: Army Sgt. William Shemin, a rifleman, posthumously received the Medal of Honor in 2015 for extraordinary heroism during World War I combat operations in France.

items.title: FBI and Partners Warn Student-Athletes of Sexual Exploitation Schemes
items.content_text: The FBI, in partnership with the NCAA, announced a joint initiative to inform student-athletes of some of the cyber-enabled tactics sexual exploitation actors use to obtain and sell their private images, and to direct them to established reporting resources.

items.title: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth Travels to Joint Base Charleston, South Carolina
items.content_text: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth will travel to Charleston, S.C., to visit Joint Base Charleston, joined by Secretary of the Air Force Troy E. Meink, Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent, South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster and Sen. Darline Graham.

items.title: Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby and Assistant Secretary of War John Noh Travel to the Philippines, Indonesia, Thailand and Cambodia
items.content_text: Undersecretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby and Assistant Secretary of War for Indo-Pacific Security Affairs John Noh departed to the Philippines, Indonesia, Thailand and Cambodia to meet with their counterparts and other senior officials.

items.title: War Department Releases Open Letter to Defense Industry Stakeholders
items.content_text: The War Department is inviting the defense industrial base and the acquisition community to provide input on ways to streamline data and audit requirements related to business systems, as part of Secretary of War Pete Hegseth's arsenal of freedom acquisition transformation strategy.

items.title: Boys & Girls Clubs Honor Military Youth
items.content_text: Five young Americans from across the War Department were honored as finalists during the Boys & Girls Clubs of America's 2026 National Military Youth of the Year celebration in the nation's capital, and one walked away with the honor and the opportunity to compete at the next level.

items.title: Multinational Partners Strengthen Regional Readiness During Exercise Panamax 2026
items.content_text: U.S. airmen joined 40 military personnel from across the Americas during Panamax 2026, a U.S. Southern Command-sponsored multinational exercise focused on an integrated approach against simulated threats to the Panama Canal and the region.

items.title: Office of Strategic Capital Signs $400 Million Conditional Loan Commitment With Sunrise Energy Metals Limited to Expand Scandium Mining Operations

items.title: Department of War Announces an $85.5 Million Agreement With Strategic Bauxite USA to Secure the Critical Refractory Grade Bauxite Supply Chain
items.content_text: The War Department announced an $85.5 million equity investment agreement with Strategic Bauxite USA, LLC to establish a secure U.S. supply chain for refractory-grade bauxite, a critical material for national defense and key industrial base sectors.

items.title: President Trump's Department of War Announces Over $80M Investment in Mining Schools at Historic Roundtable With Mining Executives

items.title: History Today, June 6: The role of signals intelligence or 'ULTRA' on D-Day
items.content_text: The term D-Day was a shorthand expression first used in World War I to denote the date an operation was to be launched. In the earlier war, officers also used H-HOUR and M-MINUTE, but these were seldom used in World War II. Because of the scope of the 1944 operation and the momentous stakes, in common parlance, “D-Day” has come to refer primarily to the landings in Normandy.
